collections.title: Banff NP 2025
collections.description: Revisited Banff over the Labour Day weekend. The park wasn’t as crowded as I expected. Popular scenic spots were busy as usual, but the hiking trails were surprisingly quiet. Sadly, with climate change, Alberta’s wildfire season has stretched into early September. Banff town was about 10 degrees above the historical average, and a light smog covered over the park. The scenery felt like only 60–70% of Banff’s full potential, but even so, it’s still one of the most beautiful parts of the Rockies.

collections.title: Presidio
collections.description: Thanks to the jet lag, I woke up at 4:30 and headed straight to Twin Peaks. The city was chilly and completely covered in fog when I reached the Christmas Tree lookout, despite checking the webcam before stepping out. The driver joked that I wouldn't spend a minute there and took me downhill. I then caught another train to Presidio/Crissy Field, where the conditions were much better, with the soft morning light being just right.

collections.title: Urbanism of Paris
collections.description: Paris really feels like peak urbanism — a city and transit system designed for everyone, not just commuters. Even during off-peak hours and weekends, trains and buses run every 3–5 minutes. The layout is also insanely well-designed, thanks to Haussmann. Green spaces are everywhere, streets and aves interweave which is far more interesting to explore on foot/bike compared to cities on a grid. The buildings all share that iconic zinc roof, brings uniformly to the skyline.

collections.title: Iceland - Snæfellsnes
collections.description: This was our last stop in Iceland. Located near the Westfjords, we took a ferry directly here. This peninsula is another picturesque destination, stretching from east to west. Its north and south shores are divided by a central mountain range, with the south coast forming a vast flat plain that gives you unobstructed views from the mountains all the way to the sea.

collections.title: Iceland – Westfjords
collections.description: Absolutely the cream of the crop in Iceland. The Westfjords feel like their own little country within Iceland. This region is geologically older than the “mainland” and deserves a dedicated tour, even though some roads are gravel. The Westfjords combine nearly every type of scenery Iceland is known for snow capped peaks alongside with bare rocky mountains, waterfalls, beaches, and ocean views all bundled together. Thanks to this unique geography, the Westfjords are known for their microclimates, much like coastal California. You don’t even have to be lucky to see rainbows, they seem to grow right out of the landscape.

collections.title: Iceland – North Iceland
collections.description: The drive from Egilsstaðir to Akureyri feels like shuttling through different worlds in minutes. You might see endless lava fields, and in the blink of an eye, they turn into lush green grasslands, only to be surrounded moments later by snow-capped mountains. It was fickle and magical. From Akureyri to Búðardalur, the landscape becomes more predictable, with endless fenced farmlands and scattered villages. This area has some of the most fertile land in Iceland. Although the fields are fenced and look empty, they’re often growing wheat-one of Iceland’s most common crops, mainly used to feed livestock like sheep and horses—taking advantage of the long summer daylight.

collections.title: Iceland – East Fjords
collections.description: The Ring Road along the East Fjords is one of the most scenic drives on the island. The town of Djúpivogur serves as the gateway to the fjords. Beyond this point lies an endless series of drives in and out of various fjords, covered in moss or bare rock, drop straight into the ocean. Sometimes, waterfalls rush from the cliffs directly into the sea, it was absolutely jaw dropping. Each fjord is geographically close, but the landscapes vary drastically.

collections.title: Iceland – Southern Coast
collections.description: The southern coast is the iconic image of Iceland that most people picture, featuring famous attractions like Seljalandsfoss, Diamond Beach, Black Sand Beach, and Glacier Lagoon—they are all over social media. The weather here changes constantly due to the meeting of Arctic and Atlantic winds, which interact with glaciers and mountains. During our first two days, we experienced completely different weather, but the vibe was immaculate.

collections.title: Spring, in general
collections.description: The spring vibe in the city is always immaculate with occasional rains, fresh greenery, and daily allergy spray. I took these photos at Brooklyn Botanic Garden, Hudson River Park, and Harsimus Cove.

collections.title: Central Park in Bloom
collections.description: Cherry Hill at Central Park was pacaked, yet the trees along the path leading there are just as good, if not better.

collections.title: NYC Postcard
collections.description: I found this spot on Google Maps where you can see iconic architectures—the Statue of Liberty, Empire State Building, and Freedom Towe all in the same frame. It's everything you would expect in a NYC postcard. The wind was strong, so I had to lower the tripod for more stability. Photos were taken at 200mm, but the images came out are as still very sharp.

collections.title: Bradley Beach
collections.description: Foggy days are rarer than sunny days. We spent the night at Bradley Beach on the Jersey Shore. The beach houses there are well maintained, and the fog added an extra layer of mystery and elegance to the scene.

collections.title: Dia Beacon
collections.description: I'm too superficial to appreciate art, especially modern art. Dia Beacon is an art museum in Beacon NY. The artworks are cool, but the most interesting part is the architecture itself - big windows with light blue curtains flowing freely like the skirts of wedding dresses, it was a truly dreamy moment.

collections.title: Brooklyn Heights
collections.description: Photos taken in Brooklyn Heights. Art Deco high rises are repurposed into residential buildings, alongside some well-maintained brownstones, tenements, and scattered abandoned factory buildings. It is a quiet but diverse neighborhood, a blend of history and modernity.

collections.title: Kunming in a Nutshell
collections.description:
This collection features photos from XunJin Street in my hometown, one of the latest developments in Kunming, filled with coffee shops seamlessly blending into a historical neighborhood. You can see people relaxing by the street, basking in Kunming’s iconic winter sunlight. This street is also a nutshell version of Kunming itself, it is slow-paced, with good weather, and people always on the lookout for drinks (tea, coffee, or anything but plain water). 
I also revisited my primary school (picture 3), which has been repurposed into a hotpot complex. I sneaked in through the public restroom, and the stairs still look just like they did back in the 2000s. But the playground has been turned into an outdoor food plaza with four subway exits shoulder to shoulder—one of the most ridiculous land redevelopments I’ve ever seen.

collections.title: Enter the Tre Cime
collections.description: Hands down the best hike of 2024. Even though the trail was completely covered in snow, we enjoyed every moment of it. The Dolomites are truly one of the most stunning parts of the Alps.

collections.title: Summer Vibes in December
collections.description:
I’ve been working on this project for a month. It’s easy to take summer-like photos during the actual summer season, but December is the farthest month from summer especially in the Northeast, where Christmas lights and cold air strip away any remaining traces of warmth. How challenging is it to find summer elements during this time of year? 
In this series, I tried to create photos with a summer vibe in the cold month of December, and make them indistinguishable from actual summer scenes, without any context. I hope you enjoy this collection.

collections.title: Urbanism of Hong Kong Pt.2
collections.description: Jan 2024 Another layover day in Hong Kong—spent about five hours between flights, took a brief walk through Central (中環). Despite recent economic hiccups and political changes, HK remains incredibly walkable, clean, diverse, and well-organized.

collections.title: Urbanism of HongKong Pt.1
collections.description: Dec 2022. First time back home after three years of COVID travel restrictions. Because of the jetlag, I woke up early, had a feast at the hotel buffet, and took a walk around North Point (北角) on Hong Kong Island. Most of my photos were taken at North Point Ferry Pier—a quiet, almost anime-like spot with layers of beams and walls creating beautiful natural frames for the ocean view.

collections.title: Seis am Schlern
collections.description: This is a more relaxed part of the Dolomites, where everything is easily accessible by cable car. The mountain weather is unpredictable, much like what I experienced in Yunnan. I hiked the mountain behind the hotel in the morning, and it was completely fogged up for hours. But at the last moment, the sun came out, shining the entire Siusi Valley.

collections.title: Mohonk Mountain
collections.description: Heading upstate or deep into New Jersey to see the fall foliage has been a must since day one. These photos were taken along the Lemon Squeeze trail at Mohonk Mountain.

collections.title: Tasa Village
collections.description: This is a Hani(哈尼族) owned village deep in Yunnan. The white ceramic tiles and green shaded windows reflect 80s Chinese architecture. Not the best looking, but they gave me a childhood flashback.

collections.title: Lake Como
collections.description: Lake Como in rain

collections.title: Florence
collections.description: Firenze (翡冷翠), a touristy town, but surprisingly home to some reasonably priced restaurants. After a late-night steak, I was walking back to the hotel when I looked up at the Florence Cathedral and suddenly found myself in tears. Later, I learned that this overwhelming excitement wasn’t unusual, it’s called Stendhal Syndrome, and fittingly, it originated right here in Florence.

collections.title: Yiliang Railway Station
collections.description: My grandparents live in Yiliang. Before the Kunming-Shiling Highway was completed, we used to take trains to visit them. The station is now completely abandoned, with lots of tourists taking pictures because it was once used as a film set. My mom took me there on the first day of 2025 to walk around and take pictures. Lots of good memories here.

collections.title: Construction in Progress
collections.description: A typical asphalt processing facility near my home.

collections.title: Sunrise in Asbury Park
collections.description: Sunrise with snow-covered beach

collections.title: Wedding in Zhima
collections.description: Zhima is a typical countryside village in Yunnan, with abundant farmland for vegetables and organically raised livestock. My grandma was born and raised here, so most of her siblings still live in the village. Before college, Zhima was our default place to spend the Spring Festival, who wouldn’t want to celebrate one of the most important holidays with the whole family gang? I used to stay for several weeks at most. This year, I made a day trip for a wedding, still the same fresh vegetables, hot dishes, and lively, chatty atmosphere everywhere. It was such a big contrast from where I live and work in Jersey.
